topic: Using std::set for Sorted Unique Collections
explanation: In C++, std::set is an associative container that stores unique elements in sorted order according to a specified comparison criterion (by default, std::less). It automatically maintains order upon insertion, ensuring no duplicates are stored. This makes it ideal for scenarios where you need a collection of unique items that are always kept sorted, facilitating efficient search, insertion, and deletion operations with logarithmic complexity. Using std::set simplifies code by eliminating the need for explicit sorting or duplicate checks after insertion, leveraging the container's inherent properties.
example_explanation: This example reads strings from standard input until EOF, inserting each into a std::set. Because std::set maintains sorted order and enforces uniqueness, duplicate inputs are automatically ignored, and the final output prints all unique strings in sorted order. This demonstrates how std::set simplifies managing sorted, duplicate-free collections in modern C++, leveraging its automatic sorting and uniqueness features.
